summary: Yunyao Zhai is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2026). They also held a post in South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

Historian, archaeologist, and Indologist Yuri Gankovsky studied at Moscow State University (~1938–1942). He later served as a teacher at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1945–1954) and as a secretary at the University of Chicago (1959–1964).

Yuri Levada studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1947–1952). His career included posts at Moscow State University (~1956–1972), the Institute of Sociology (~1966–1972), VTSIOM (~1988–2003), the Levada Center (~2003–2006), and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.

Yuri Parfionovich worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1948–1953) and under George de Roerich (~1957–1960) and Bidia Dandaron (~1965–1972). He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies in 1953.
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from ~1937 to 1940 and later served as a professor there from ~1965 to 1987.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Yusho Miyasaka studied at Chisan College and Tohoku University, under Shoko Watanabe. He held posts at Koyasan University, served as Professor Emeritus at Nagoya University, and held positions at Chisan Denpōin and Shuchiin University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Yusho Wakahara studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Hanazono University (attested 1987) and Ryukoku University as an associate professor (attested 1987–1999) and professor (attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, serving as Emeritus Professor at Doho University (~1968–2005).

Yutaka Hirata, a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, earned a doctorate from Kyushu University. He worked at the Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1959–1978), Kyushu University (1971–1995), and Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University (~1995–2005).

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Yutaka Iwamoto studied at Kyoto University under multiple teachers and doctoral supervisors. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Tokyo University of Science, Tokai University (~1967–1974), Kyoto Tachibana University (~1974–1980), and Soka University (~1980–1988).

Yutaka Kanazawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2010. Kanazawa's studies were supervised by Shoryu Katsura and Masaaki Noni, alongside instruction from Kōgi Kudara, Hōgei Mitsukawa, and Isao Shimizu.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar Yutaka Kawasaki studied under Seio Okuda. Kawasaki has held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yutaka Ochihara specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania under teachers including Louis Renou and Atsuuji Ashikaga. He held professorial posts at Kyoto University (1957; 1972–1986) and Collège de France (1985).

Yutaka Takagi, a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studied at Tokyo University of Literature and Science from ~1948 to 1951. He later served as a professor at Rissho University from ~1968 to 1999.

Yutaka Yoshida studied at Tokyo University of Education, Hitotsubashi University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. Specializing in history, archaeology, Japanology, and linguistics, he held long-term posts at Hitotsubashi University (1983–2018) and a professorship at Kyoto University (2006).

Yutaka Yuda was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Hajime Nakamura and earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as an associate professor at Kyoritsu College of Pharmacy (1969) and Kanagawa University (1975–2003).

Sinologist and linguist Yutang Lin studied at St. John's University, Harvard University, and the University of Leipzig under doctoral supervisor August Conrady. He later held an academic post at Peking University from ~1923 to 1926.

Yuto Kawamura is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University (2015–2018) and held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 2013–2026), the University of Oxford (attested 2019), and the University of Tokyo (attested 2026).

Sinologist and philosopher Yuzo Mizoguchi studied at the University of Tokyo, Nagoya University under Yoshitaka Iriya, and Kyushu University. He held academic posts at Saitama, Hitotsubashi, Tokyo, and Daito Bunka universities, and was an honorary professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Yün-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and later worked as a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
